verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is the README's claim that Zero "does not track, collect, or sell your data in any way," plus self-hosting, which gives some control over where mail data lives. The evidence never mentions blocking senders' tracking pixels, by default or otherwise, which is the core of the story. Missing for 10: tracking-pixel or remote-image blocking (default-on), a detailed data-handling or privacy policy (especially for AI features processing mail), and any independent corroboration.
